Hi Harj and Jon, 

Hope you are well. We would like to clarify a few things that we observed in production. 

1. CNDC movements - We see that SME_SUPPLIER_CODE and SME_STK_CONDITION_CODE are the same for 4 movements. As per our understanding, these codes should be different. They are different for other CNDC movements, but they are the same only for these four movements.

2.  XFER movements: Our current implementation groups XFER movements and uses the lowest SME_INT_LINE_NO for a unique record. However, we have seen 6 records where, for the lowest SME_INT_LINE_NO, SME_FROM_WAREHOUSE and SME_TO_WAREHOUSE are the same. This causes us to stop processing that movement. Here also logic works fine for other XFER records but see these kinds of differences for these 6 movements only.

Attaching the documents with all 10 movements that look different from other movements 
Please refer to the calidus movements sheet for the actual data.

From: Harj Lasher

Cc: Jon Brittle <Jon.Brittle@abc.com>; Jnanasriharsha Dattada <dj@abc.co.uk>; Sudip Roy <sudip.roy@abc.co.uk>; Apteansupport <Apteansupport@abc.com>; Arindam Sen <arindam.sen@abc.co.uk>
Subject: RE: [EXTERNAL] Reconciling Calidus movements

 

Hi,

 

CLSU can do either a write on or write off depending on the Suspense stock position.

 

When it is negative (e.g. -23 as in case below) a write on is performed i.e. physical and suspense is increased by the inverse of the suspense quantity (e.g. +23 as in case below).

 

When it is positive a write off is performed i.e. physical and suspense is decreased by the suspense quantity.

 

To distinguish write on or write off action for a CLSU stock movement extract record you can refer to the SME_STATUS column (i.e. 0 = stock reduction; 1 = stock increase).

 

Regards,

Harj

On Thu, 23 Apr 2026 at 11:28, Harj Lasher <Harj.Lasher@abc.com> wrote:

Hi,

 

1)) The table to query is the STOCK_MOVEMENT_EXTRACT.

See below the query for selecting the extracted movements for the 14th to 16th for SKU 119135.

The output includes the Run Id (SME_RUN_ID), this is included in the name of physical extract file i.e. sme_2973_20260415_03500022.csv and sme_2991_20260415_08200027.csv.

Please query this table with caution as it contains a large number of records and we don’t want to impact the overall performance of Calidus.

 

select * from stock_movement_extract

where sme_movement_date in (20260414, 20260415, 20260416)

and sme_product_code = '119135'

and sme_processed_ind = 1

and sme_ignored_ind = 0

order by sme_id;

 

 



11170081   20260415   3483516      2973          1            0             20260415        3500022         544            119135                73D     GIGD

11202583   20260415   8141691      2991          1            0             20260415        8200027         544           119135                73D     PUT

 

 

2)) From the output above you can see the GIGD followed by the PUT movements for SKU 119135.

The GIGD was exported in extract sme_2973_20260415_03500022.csv.

The PUT was exported in extract sme_2991_20260415_08200027.csv.

Hi Harj and Jon,

 

Hope you are well. We would like to clarify a couple of points we found during validation and reconciliation between Calidus and Stock Master. 

Calidus movements: We are trying to match the movements received by SM (Stock Master) vs movements in Calidus. Could you please provide us an extract of all movements for April 14, 15 and 16th for SKUs: 152889, 119135, 435228. Attached is the list of movements we received in SM for reference. Please let us know if there is a table we can refer to for querying this view by individual SKUs. 
GIGD movement: We noticed that for SKU 152889, SM received 3 PUT transactions of 900 each (In the attached file). However, there wasn't any GIGD (Goods Receipting) transaction before any of these PUT transactions. Our understanding was that GIGD would always precede the PUT (putaway) transaction. We noticed a similar issue with SKU 119135, where SM received 1 PUT transaction without any preceding GIGD transaction.
Let us know if you have any questions. Thank you

 

Kind regards

Ashutosh
